chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Statement of the Exalted
So when they neglected what they had been reminded of, We delivered those who forbade evil

He said: There were three types. A type who were with the command and commanded others, so they were saved; and a type who were with the command but did not command others, so they were metamorphosed into dust; and a type who were not with the command and did not command others, so they perished.
ai.seo_question: How did the three groups of people respond to the command to forbid evil according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the fate of the people mentioned in Surah Al-A'raf by categorizing them into three distinct groups based on their internal conviction and external action regarding 'forbidding evil' (Nahy an al-Munkar). This hadith highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the necessity of both accepting the command and actively enforcing it, distinguishing between those who were merely transformed into dust for passive compliance and those who perished for total neglect.

en.hubeali: H 14599 – Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Amro Bin Usman, from Abdullah Bin Al-Mugheira, from Talha Bin Zayd, who has narrated the following:
Abu Abdullahasws regarding the Statement of the Highazwj:
“[7:165] So when they neglected what they had been reminded of, We delivered those who forbade evil”.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There were of three types – A type who were with the commands and they commanded others, so they were Rescued; and a type who were with the commands but they did not command others, so they were metamorphosed as particles; and a type who were not with the command and did not command others, so they perished’.
